title: fix(core,components,fields): the shared date path refuses a nonexistent calendar day (objectui#10026)
body:
Fixes #10026

Clause-②: yes — `@object-ui/core` gains one export, `isRealCalendarDate(dateOnly)`, MOVED from `@object-ui/components`' filter builder, where it was module-private. The filter builder imports it from core; no second implementation exists. No signature moves: `toDisplayDate`, `formatDate`, `formatRelativeDate`, `formatDateTime` and `formatDateTimeCompactParts` keep theirs, and each changes its answer for ONE input class only (a date-only value naming a day its month does not have) to its EXISTING answer for an unparsable value. Nothing is removed, renamed or retyped, and `@object-ui/fields` does not re-export the new name.

Ruling: comment 5749269396 on the card (option A). Implemented in session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01BP8CMtACxTdLjqR6rhd33C`.

## What was wrong (measured on `origin/main` `6099dd870`)

- The engine accepts a nonexistent day and rolls it forward. `Date.parse` returns an instant for `2026-02-30` (March 2nd), `2024-02-31` (March 2nd), `2025-02-29` (March 1st) and `2026-04-31` (May 1st). It returns `NaN` only for a bad month or a day outside 01-31: `2026-13-01`, `2026-02-32`, `2026-02-00`.
- So `formatDate('2026-02-30')` rendered `Mar 2`, while the filter builder's module-private `isRealCalendarDate` refused the same value at the authoring boundary. Two green pins held the roll in place: `agrees with the list cell on a rolled-over date instead of second-guessing it` (dataset-format date suite) and `still ROLLS a well-shaped impossible day, and now rolls to the same day everywhere` (the objectui#10110 zone suite).
- The move surfaced a latent defect in the moved body. `Date.UTC(year, ...)` maps years 0-99 onto 1900+y, so the function answered `false` for `0026-08-01`. Refusing through that body as it stood would have dashed every year below 100, which the display path renders and the zone suite pins (`keeps a two-digit year out of the 1900s`).

## The route, with each dispatch assumption measured

- **A3, the move.** No core helper already made this judgement. `toDisplayDate`'s date-only rebuild reads the parts but judges nothing. `isRealCalendarDate` now sits beside `toDisplayDate` and reuses that module's `ISO_DATE_ONLY_RE`, not a third spelling of the `YYYY-MM-DD` shape. It reads the year with `setUTCFullYear`, which has no 1900+y mapping. The filter builder's three call sites are unchanged; its `DATE_ONLY_PATTERN`, used only by the moved function, went with it.
- **A2, the marker.** Read, not designed. Every function in `date-display.ts` answers an unparsable value with `—`, and `formatDateTimeCompactParts` answers `null`. The refusal reuses exactly those answers. The new pins compare against each function's own answer for `not-a-date`, read at run time.
- **A1, where the refusal lives: IN the shared parse step.** `toDisplayDate` returns an Invalid Date for such a value, so all four formatters refuse the same way.
  - ⚠️ **This departs from the dispatch's fallback clause, and it is stated here so it can be overruled.** Refusing in the parse step moves two faces the ruling does not name, the History tab (`auditHistoryDisplay`) and the record summary chip. Each goes from a rolled date to the stored string, which is its existing face for an unparsable value.
  - The fallback was to refuse only in the formatters, beside the parse step. It was measured as unworkable for a face the ruling DOES name: the list cell. Four field faces catch an unparsable value with `EmptyValue`. Each claimed to be co-extensive with `formatDate`'s dash by re-spelling its parse as `new Date(value)`, and that spelling accepts `2026-02-30`. With the refusal outside the parse step, those faces would either paint a bare dash or re-decide the refusal with their own copy of the date-only shape test. The bare dash is the objectui#8581 / objectui#8809 defect back, and a third marker shape, which the ruling forbids. The copy is a second decision site. With the refusal inside the parse step, the guards read `toDisplayDate` and are co-extensive by construction.
- **A4, datetime-shaped values.** Measured: the engine rolls them too (`2026-02-30T10:00:00Z` parses as March 2nd 10:00Z). They are NOT refused here. The ruling's operative bullet names date-only values, and the most visible datetime face (`DateTimeCellRenderer`) hands its formatters an already-parsed `Date`, which no parse step can refuse. This is raised as an open question in the report, and it is listed under Acceptance notes.

## Changes

- `packages/core/src/utils/date-display.ts`: `isRealCalendarDate` moved in and exported, `toDisplayDate` now refuses, docs updated.
- `packages/components/src/custom/filter-builder.tsx`: the definition and its pattern are removed; the function is imported from `@object-ui/core`.
- `packages/fields/src/index.tsx` (`DateCellRenderer`, `DateTimeCellRenderer`), `widgets/DateField.tsx`, `widgets/FormulaField.tsx`: the validity guards read `toDisplayDate`, spelled identically in the two sibling cells.
  - The `date` cell's overdue predicate reads that same `Date`.
  - The `datetime` cell still hands its formatters the engine's `new Date(safe)`, so its instant is unchanged. The `date` cell's `title` is unchanged too.
- `packages/core/src/utils/dataset-format.ts`: comments only. The two notes that asserted the roll and called this card open now describe the refusal.
- Pins:
  - The dataset-format pin is rewritten with its rationale, not deleted: the list cell and the measure still agree, now on the refusal. The measure makes no refusal of its own; its guard still lets the value through to the shared path.
  - The objectui#10110 zone case is rewritten to pin the refusal in two zones. Its measured-directions table is annotated, not re-derived.
  - New: `date-display.impossibleDay-10026.test.ts` and `date-carriers.impossibleDay-10026.test.tsx`.
- `.changeset/10026-refuse-impossible-calendar-day.md`: core minor; components and fields patch.
- The pending `date-only-calendar-day-10110.md` said the path keeps rolling such a day. Both entries publish in the same release, so that sentence is corrected (prose only, frontmatter untouched).

**Files beyond the claim's surface:** the three `@object-ui/fields` sources, the objectui#10110 zone test, the `dataset-format.ts` comments and the 10110 changeset. This change made a statement or a guard in each one false.

## Acceptance notes

- **C, refusing at the producing boundary (import or API).** Carrier: 承接者:无. No card or pull request read in this session carries a producer-side date-validity refusal. Values already stored are what this change addresses.
- **Datetime-shaped values still roll (A4).** `formatDateTime('2026-02-30T10:00:00Z')` renders `Mar 2, 2026, 10:00 AM`. `DateTimeCellRenderer` and the `datetime` arm of `formatMeasureDate` are the same. The `ISO_DATETIME_RE` note in `dataset-format.ts` says so.
- **Faces that build their own `Date` before formatting never meet the refusal.** `GridField`'s sub-grid `date` column builds `new Date(y, m - 1, d)` and still renders `Mar 2` for `2026-02-30`. Its unparsable face is the raw stored string (objectui#3569).
- **Two faces answer "not a date" two ways.** `data-table` and `ObjectGrid`'s key-name date sniff guard with `Date.parse` and show the raw string for `NaN`, but a nonexistent day reaches `formatDate` and shows `—`. This is the same shape the ruling accepted for the dataset measure.
- **The History tab and the summary chip change face.** A nonexistent date-only day now shows as the stored string in both, their existing unparsable face (see A1).
- **The filter builder keeps a year below 100.** A year below 100 (`0026-08-01`) now converts into a date column instead of clearing, a consequence of the year fix.
- **No README change.** The core README documents none of the date-display exports, and objectui#10183 did not add `toDisplayDate` there. It is not extended here.
- **Incidence is still unmeasured**, carried from the ruling.

  - `8581-date-cell-unparsable-value` and `8809-date-carrier-unparsable`: "the guard reproduces `formatDate`'s own parse" is now literally true.
  - `dataset-format-8263-impossible-date-prose`: its frontmatter is empty, so it publishes nothing. It describes the roll as pinned, and it is left as a historical declaration.
